epistemic_role: Bounded deterministic interface diagnosis following frozen J6B-D1; not a new stochastic or risk study
question: Does the integrated public schedule-to-action path's terminal-residual flag equal an independently recomputed boundary of the final hidden physical chain XOR the latest committed public full-snapshot Pauli-frame estimate, and how do late faults and readout-only flips differ?
program_alignment: Lab 005 fault-tolerance prerequisite: establish which public decision and private scoring semantics can explain the D1 high-residual pattern before considering more sampling.
research_basis: Existing D4 projector-level five-round L=2 channel, J6B public E1/E2 interface, and unchanged Boolean-union private score. No new physical channel, scorer, schedule, external method or dependency.
competing_explanations: A late physical fault after the final effective commit leaves a genuine terminal residual even when earlier actions were correct.
A readout-only flip can create a public action or defer without a matching physical fault, yielding a different residual or fail-closed path.
The frame/scorer implementation disagrees with the independently recomputed final-chain identity, indicating a correctness defect rather than evidence for either physical explanation.
fixed_channel_and_geometry: Paper-normalized periodic D4 honeycomb L=2, five readout rounds, four physical transitions; p_data=p_syndrome=p_fp=p_fn=p_confuse=0 except one explicitly supplied deterministic syndrome-readout bit. Existing first-observation seeds (10,11,12,13,14), herald uniforms 0.5, and fixed SHA-256 keys derived from labels physical/first/second; no RNG history generation.
public_interface: Use run_e1_policy_matrix on each causal first record, both syndrome_only and heralded modes and all immediate, fixed_delay_1, jit_lyons_brown and explicitly noncausal offline_full_history branches. An even full-snapshot flux action is an absolute cumulative frame; same-round duplicates collapse and the latest action supersedes earlier actions. An odd temporal-boundary handoff is no physical correction. Public second record is action-conditioned, full-binary and relation-free. Hidden physical chain and post-flux relation enter only the private generation/scoring audit.
score_and_denominator: Keep evaluate_schedule_arm's unconditional one-row-per-mode/schedule/history Boolean union of physical winding, union winding, charge winding and terminal residual; failed-closed counts as loss. The independent residual oracle is boundary(final physical XOR latest public full-snapshot flux correction), with zero correction when no physical commit. Do not redefine this scorer or condition risk on scored rows.
integrity_and_acceptance: All pinned source and frozen J6B/D1 hashes match before and after execution; exactly five supplied histories and 40 public arm evaluations are retained, including failed-closed rows.

For every scored row, independently recomputed terminal residual matches the row flag and logical_failure equals the four unchanged Boolean flags; commit rounds and latest public correction are self-consistent.

Every physical commit has an action-bound public second record with relation-free public charge action; no private support, relation, physical chain, winding or score field appears in the public request/completion dictionaries.

Early and early-plus-late histories have identical public requests/actions through round 3; a future fault cannot change an earlier causal decision. Replaying the full 40-arm matrix is byte-identical.
Classify late fault, readout flip, cancellation and early fault by observed row/status/commit trace without imposing an expected schedule ranking or causal attribution to the stochastic D1 cohort.
stop_rule: Fail closed on any hash, public/private leakage, replay, prefix, frame identity or denominator mismatch. On a failed gate preserve a censored machine-readable result, do not change the source or rescore J6B in this tick. Passing only supports deterministic interface consistency or a localized counterexample, not a mechanism fraction, conditional risk, JIT benefit or threshold.
